properties.areaDesc: Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20 Nm
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 11 at 3:07PM EDT until September 11 at 3:30PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
For the following areas...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...

At 306 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing waterspouts
were located along a line extending from 6 nm east of St George
Island to near K Tower, moving east at 5 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life jackets.
Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots...suddenly higher
waves...frequent lightning...and heavy downpours. Make sure
all on board are wearing life jackets.

Locations impacted include...
O Tower, C Tower, St George Island, K Tower, and Apalachicola.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 11 at 12:19PM MST until September 11 at 12:45PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 119 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over Leupp, or 25
miles northwest of Winslow, moving northeast at 10 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Leupp and Sunrise.

This includes State Route 99 between mile markers 65 and 71.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 11 at 2:17PM CDT until September 11 at 3:00PM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA
properties.description:
SVRSHV

The National Weather Service in Shreveport has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
East Central McCurtain County in southeastern Oklahoma...

* Until 300 PM CDT.

* At 217 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 8 miles northeast
of Broken Bow, or 17 miles west of De Queen, moving southeast at 10
mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Eagletown.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

If on or near a lake, get away from the water and move indoors or
inside a vehicle. Remember, lightning can strike out to 15 miles from
the parent thunderstorm. If you can hear thunder, you are close
enough to be struck by lightning. Move to safe shelter now! Do not be
caught on the water in a thunderstorm.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 11 at 9:20AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From late Sunday night until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Friday the stage was 7.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Monday morning and continue rising to 12.2 feet Monday morning.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.2
feet on 11/24/1997.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 930 PM EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT FROM LATE SUNDAY NIGHT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE
